Subject: Elevated 5xxs from AtlasX-7b for BrightLayer - seeing customer-facing failures

Hi Rachel,

Heads up — over the last ~20 minutes we've seen a sharp rise in 5xx and timeout responses coming from model AtlasX-7b across a subset of our queries (batch size ~8, typical prompt lengths 1k-2k tokens). It's impacting multi-tenant endpoints that drive our ingestion pipeline; error rate climbed to ~9% for a few min.

Samples attached (atlasx_sample_1, atlasx_sample_2). Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing an elevated error rate on AtlasX-7b in us-west? We have a go-live at 1500 PDT and this is blocking some upstream workers.

Thanks — Jordan

Hi Jordan — thanks for the report and the samples. We see correlated spikes in 5xx and timeouts for AtlasX-7b in us-west over the same window. Our on-call is triaging. Quick mitigation steps we can apply immediately:

- Route BrightLayer traffic to the AtlasX-7b-fallback variant (quantized) for the next 30 mins — minimal quality difference; should remove 5xxs.
- Increase request-level timeout to 45s for affected endpoints.
- Apply prefix-KV cache warm for long-running sessions where possible.

I have CC'd Ben (Support) and Marissa (Platform Ops) to coordinate the routing change and log collection. Ben — can you enable the fallback and notify Jordan when done? Marissa — please collect the KV cache dump and the runtime trace for the 09:00–09:30 window and attach. I will follow up with a full recovery note + postmortem timeline.

Rachel

Subject: AtlasX-7b — incident resolved and postmortem link (BrightLayer)

Jordan —

Thanks again for the quick report and patience. Final update and summary below.

What happened (high level):
- Between 09:00–09:30 PDT on Apr 10 we observed an elevated rate of 5xx and request timeouts for AtlasX-7b in our us-west serving pool. The root cause was a KV-cache eviction regression triggered by a recent model runtime change plus an edge case in our continuous-batching logic that caused certain long-prefix requests to attempt a hot-reload path and hit a race. This produced transient GPU memory pressure and a small class of requests (larger context + batch) to fail with 5xx.

Impact:
- BrightLayer: brief error rate peak ~9% for ~25 minutes. Some ingestion workers retried and caused increased latency on your side; no customer data exfiltration.

Mitigations applied:
- 09:22 PDT: Routed BrightLayer traffic to atlasx-7b-quant fallback (no 5xx observed afterward).
- 09:34 PDT: Increased per-request timeout and applied short-term batch-size caps for your tenant.
- 09:40 PDT: Reverted the runtime change to the KV-cache eviction strategy and applied a hotfix to the batching guard.

Resolution:
- 09:50 PDT: Error rates returned to baseline; no further escalations observed.

Next steps / commitments:
- We have posted a formal postmortem (link below) that includes timelines, root cause analysis, and the permanent fix plan.
- Permanent fix: change will land in the next release (canary next week, full rollout mid-May). We will share a schedule for the canary and invite BrightLayer to a verification window.
- As a precautionary measure, we are crediting BrightLayer with one day of service usage for the impacted endpoints; finance will follow up.

Artifacts attached / links:
- Attached: atlasx7b-kvcache-dump.tar.gz, atlasx7b-error-sample.log.txt, postmortem-atlasx7b-20280412.pdf
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-INC-4521
- Postmortem: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-postmortem

If you'd like a quick sync (15 min) to walk through the postmortem, I'm available today 16:00–17:00 PDT or tomorrow morning. Let me know what works.

Apologies for the disruption — we're prioritizing preventing recurrence.

Best,
Rachel Kim
